paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Teacher looks at life under the sun and says out loud what most of us would rather not. There is one fate for everyone, and nobody knows what lies ahead (Ecclesiastes 9:1-3). He isn't saying life doesn't matter. He's saying we don't run the clock, and the righteous and the wise, along with their deeds, are "in God's hands" (Ecclesiastes 9:1).

So what do you do with that? You LIVE, baker. The Teacher says there is hope for anyone among the living, and he says to eat your bread with joy, because "God has already approved your works" (Ecclesiastes 9:4, 7). Enjoy the people God gave you and the fleeting days He gave you, because this is your portion in life (Ecclesiastes 9:9). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I promise you, a day with warm ovens beats a day with dust.

Then he hands you the other half: whatever you find to do with your hands, do it "with all your might," for in Sheol there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom (Ecclesiastes 9:10). He also says time and chance happen to all, so the swift and the strong don't get a guarantee (Ecclesiastes 9:11). That means you can't hold your life together by being the fastest or the smartest. You can bring your whole heart to today's work and joy, and leave tomorrow in God's hands. And the Teacher isn't finished yet, so the teaching isn't over.
